open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity
open_points.text:
On 2026-10-31 the owner answered the draft's questions: the object has no
identity of its own (M02; "object ids" in R0-50 and R0-80 is a slip, to be
corrected there by R0-86), and the
proposals under M01, M04 and M10 are accepted as written.
open_points.question: Did the accepted 2026-10-31 M10 decision make MigrationClosure the value embedded in StoreHistory described by the accepted draft, or the independently persisted entity that the changed M10 attributes to that same decision?
options: Keep the accepted draft decision: MigrationClosure is a value embedded in StoreHistory.
Replace it with a new decision: MigrationClosure is an entity whose identity is the accepted file digest.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the changed declaration as a replacement decision and model MigrationClosure as a digest-identified entity.

witness.initial: A successful VPS import has produced a migration closure.
events: A later model-closure author translates the accepted 2026-10-31 M10 proposal.
Another author translates the changed M10 identity and persistence passages.
outcomes: The closure is emitted as a value embedded in store history.
The closure is emitted as an independently persisted entity keyed by the file digest.
witness.observer: Repository, contract and migration implementers see different model identities and persistence ownership.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity across store histories
open_points.text:
It is identified by the digest of the file the import accepted, the one
identity it has (codex round-04 T1); Registry mints no identifier for it.
open_points.question: Is the digest a globally sufficient identity, making acceptance of the same file after a pre-import backup restore a continuation or recreation of the same entity, or is MigrationClosure identity scoped by the store or store history as well as the digest?
options: The digest alone identifies the entity across all stores and restored histories.
Identity is the pair of store or store-history identity and digest.
Each successful import creates a new entity, while the digest is only a fact or natural key.
open_points.default_guess: Scope the entity identity to the store history and use the digest as its local identifier.

witness.initial: Store history H1 accepts file digest D, then the store is lost and restored from a backup made before that import.
events: The owner submits the same file with digest D to the restored store.
Registry successfully imports it because the restored store has no closure.
outcomes: The new closure is the same digest-identified entity as the lost closure.
The new closure is a distinct entity belonging to the restored store's new history, despite having digest D.
witness.observer: Persistence and audit implementations disagree whether two successful imports created one entity or two.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure and M05 ArtifactPointer
open_points.text:
Substitution: a closure is not interchangeable with an equal value elsewhere:
it is the record a pointer the import brought in names as its publisher (M05)
and the audit entry of the import names (M09), and the record whose presence
refuses a second import (R0-79).
open_points.question: Does an imported pointer name the MigrationClosure entity as its publisher, or must it name the acting owner as required by R0-88's statement that pointers record who published them and that only the agent through Kernel or the owner publishes?
options: Imported pointers name MigrationClosure as publisher.
Imported pointers name the owner as publisher; MigrationClosure is separate provenance.
ArtifactPointer has separate actor-publisher and migration-provenance facts.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the owner as publisher and add a separate migration-provenance reference if that reference is required.

witness.initial: The VPS export contains an artifact pointer selected for import.
events: Registry creates the MigrationClosure and imports the pointer.
A caller later reads the pointer's publisher information.
outcomes: The pointer identifies MigrationClosure as its publisher.
The pointer identifies the owner who confirmed the import as its publisher.
witness.observer: The owner or an authorized artifact reader sees different publisher identity.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure reads
open_points.text:
Registry must remember it to
refuse a second import; nothing else of the migration is a Registry record —
the export file's format is States 5 and 6 (R0-72), and the import's results
are Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers like any other.
open_points.question: Which product actions may read MigrationClosure: only the import guard and backup machinery, or also an owner-facing import-status read, pointer reads, audit reads, or another operation?
options: It is internal state read only when checking an import and when persisting or backing up the store.
The owner can read the closure and its facts through a product action.
Other models may reference it, but no product action returns the closure itself.
open_points.default_guess: Keep it internal: the import action checks its presence, persistence and backup copy it, and no product answer returns the closure itself.

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence existing-store lifecycle
open_points.text:
Registry makes it,
with number 0, in the transaction that makes a new, empty store (State 2 A17
rule 5) and never makes a second one.
open_points.question: How does a pre-existing nonempty store that already has audit history acquire its required exactly-one AuditSequence when this model is introduced?
options: Adopt or migrate the already durable counter while preserving its current last number.
Derive an initial value from the greatest audit-entry number.
Refuse to open a store without an AuditSequence.
Create it at 0 even for an existing store.
open_points.default_guess: Migrate or adopt the existing durable counter and preserve its last assigned number.

witness.initial: An existing store contains audit entries through sequence 41 but predates the M12 model record.
events: The release introducing M12 opens the store.
A product change appends the next audit entry.
outcomes: Initialization preserves 41 and the new entry receives the next unused number.
Initialization creates 0, refuses startup, or derives a different current value.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log sees either uninterrupted numbering or a reuse, discontinuity, or unavailable Registry.

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence identity on restore
open_points.text:
A restored store holds this record as the backup holds it, the same
record continued; Registry neither knows nor records that the store was
restored.
open_points.question: Since M12 is identified by the store that holds it while R0-89 says a restored store begins its own history from the backup, is the restored AuditSequence the same entity, or a new entity initialized with the backed-up number?
options: It is the same entity continued across backup and restore.
It is a new store-history entity whose initial number is copied from the backup.
Store identity itself continues across restore, so the entity remains the same; this must be stated explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: Treat store identity and its AuditSequence entity as continuing across disaster recovery, while later events form a new history branch.

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence source of truth
open_points.question: Is the independently persisted AuditSequence record authoritative for the last number, or must the current audit entries be treated as the source of truth even after old entries are erased?
options: AuditSequence is authoritative; appends are the only actions allowed to change it.
The greatest surviving audit-entry number is authoritative.
The complete historical append stream is authoritative even though Registry no longer retains all of it.
open_points.default_guess: Make the AuditSequence record authoritative and state that audit appends atomically advance it.

witness.initial: The durable AuditSequence is 100 and the owner erases all retained entries numbered through 90; the erasure itself appends entry 101.
events: The owner later erases older entries again, leaving only a small suffix.
A new significant change appends another audit entry.
outcomes: The implementation reads AuditSequence and assigns a number greater than every number ever used.
The implementation derives authority from surviving entries and may lower or reuse a number after erasure.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log and any backup verifier sees whether sequence numbers remain globally unreused within the store history.

open_points.subject: State 1 model field declarations
open_points.text:
Field names, types,
formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay
mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0,
"Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).
open_points.question: Replace the deferral of model field names and types with complete typed field declarations for every State 1 model, including M10 MigrationClosure and M12 AuditSequence.
